weeks.title: Node, Values, and Output
weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a Node receipt calculator.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse const, let, number, template literal, strict equality so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a Node receipt calculator.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 1 Skill Check, then preview the a Node receipt calculator contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Node, Values, and Output Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines const. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned
a block-scoped binding that may be reassigned

questions.explanation: const means a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned; it is used to store an unchanged tax rate. Avoid this mistake: assume the object held by const cannot change.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to store an unchanged tax rate. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: const is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to assume the object held by const cannot change.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for let, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: expect decimal money to be exact in every case
use single quotes and expect interpolation
use var by habit in new beginner code
use = or rely on coercing equality

questions.explanation: let means a block-scoped binding that may be reassigned; it is used to update a running total. Avoid this mistake: use var by habit in new beginner code.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to use var by habit in new beginner code. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: let is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use var by habit in new beginner code.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates number?
questions.explanation: number means JavaScript numeric values; it is used to calculate price * quantity. Avoid this mistake: expect decimal money to be exact in every case.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: calculate price * quantity?
questions.explanation: number is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect decimal money to be exact in every case.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain template literal before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned
a block-scoped binding that may be reassigned

questions.explanation: template literal means backtick text with embedded expressions; it is used to write `Total: ${total}`. Avoid this mistake: use single quotes and expect interpolation.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "backtick text with embedded expressions". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: template literal is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use single quotes and expect interpolation.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that strict equality was misunderstood?

options.label: assume the object held by const cannot change
use var by habit in new beginner code
expect decimal money to be exact in every case
use = or rely on coercing equality

questions.explanation: strict equality means comparison without type coercion; it is used to check choice === "1". Avoid this mistake: use = or rely on coercing equality.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—use = or rely on coercing equality—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: strict equality is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use = or rely on coercing equality.

builds.title: Microbuild: a Node receipt calculator
builds.outcome: A working, tested a Node receipt calculator.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a Node receipt calculator. Required behavior: demonstrate const, let, number, template literal, strict equality; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a Node receipt calculator: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make const, let, number visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using template literal and strict equality. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—use = or rely on coercing equality—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a Node receipt calculator through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: const, let, number, template literal, strict equality.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving const and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "use = or rely on coercing equality" and change one cause at a time.

skillCheck.title: Input and Decisions Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 2 guide defines process.argv. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: turning numeric text into a number

questions.explanation: process.argv means command-line arguments supplied to Node; it is used to read a fare zone argument. Avoid this mistake: expect browser prompt() in Node.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to read a fare zone argument. Which concept from the Week 2 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: process.argv is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect browser prompt() in Node.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for Number conversion, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: write a condition that returns text instead of boolean reasoning
confuse || with a default in every context

questions.explanation: Number conversion means turning numeric text into a number; it is used to use Number(rawAge). Avoid this mistake: add numeric text before conversion.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to add numeric text before conversion. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: Number conversion is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to add numeric text before conversion.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 2 guide correctly demonstrates if statement?
questions.explanation: if statement means conditional execution; it is used to choose adult or child fare. Avoid this mistake: write a condition that returns text instead of boolean reasoning.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: choose adult or child fare?
questions.explanation: if statement is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to write a condition that returns text instead of boolean reasoning.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain logical operator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: turning numeric text into a number

questions.explanation: logical operator means combining boolean conditions; it is used to require valid age && valid zone. Avoid this mistake: confuse || with a default in every context.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "combining boolean conditions". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: logical operator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to confuse || with a default in every context.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that NaN check was misunderstood?

options.label: write a condition that returns text instead of boolean reasoning

questions.explanation: NaN check means detecting failed numeric conversion; it is used to use Number.isNaN(value). Avoid this mistake: compare value === NaN.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—compare value === NaN—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: NaN check is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to compare value === NaN.

skillCheck.title: Loops and Arrays Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 3 guide defines array. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: array means an ordered collection; it is used to store weekly scores. Avoid this mistake: use separate numbered variables.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to store weekly scores. Which concept from the Week 3 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: array is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use separate numbered variables.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for for...of, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: use for...in when values are needed
expect the first position to be 1
expect push to return the new array

questions.explanation: for...of means iteration over iterable values; it is used to visit each score. Avoid this mistake: use for...in when values are needed.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to use for...in when values are needed. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: for...of is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use for...in when values are needed.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 3 guide correctly demonstrates index?

options.label: use push to append a score

questions.explanation: index means a zero-based array position; it is used to read scores[0]. Avoid this mistake: expect the first position to be 1.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: read scores[0]?
questions.explanation: index is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect the first position to be 1.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain accumulator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: accumulator means state updated through a loop; it is used to sum scores into total. Avoid this mistake: declare total inside the loop.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "state updated through a loop". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: accumulator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to declare total inside the loop.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that array method was misunderstood?

options.label: expect push to return the new array
use for...in when values are needed
expect the first position to be 1

questions.explanation: array method means a built-in collection operation; it is used to use push to append a score. Avoid this mistake: expect push to return the new array.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—expect push to return the new array—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: array method is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect push to return the new array.

skillCheck.title: Functions and Objects Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 4 guide defines function. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: a local name for a function input
sending a result to the caller
named properties grouped as one value
reusable behavior with inputs and output

questions.explanation: function means reusable behavior with inputs and output; it is used to write calculateAverage(scores). Avoid this mistake: mix all program input and output into every function.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to write calculateAverage(scores). Which concept from the Week 4 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: function is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to mix all program input and output into every function.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for parameter, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: log a value callers must reuse
depend on property order for meaning
